findings.message: Helm will delete CustomResourceDefinition/default/miniojobs.job.min.io. A templated custom resource definition that the new chart does not render is removed, and Kubernetes then deletes every object of that kind.
ClusterRole/default/minio-operator-role adds rules that the current chart did not have.
Chart default `operator.image.tag` changed from `v6.0.1` to `v7.1.1` and the rendered objects differ.
The pod template of Deployment/stageproof-check/minio-operator changed at spec.template.metadata.labels.app.kubernetes.io/version. The pods will restart. A restart is normal for an upgrade.

findings.detail: Stageproof does not read that project's upgrade notes. A skip of more than one minor version, or a new major version, is named here and does not block.
findings.message: Chart version moves from 6.0.1 to 7.1.1, a new major version.

findings.detail: This is the chart's declared application version. It is not a test that the registry tag exists.
findings.message: appVersion moves from v6.0.1 to v7.1.1. The image that the chart runs may change with it.

findings.detail: The render names a different image, including images on custom resources and images passed as container arguments. Whether that tag exists is a separate check.
findings.message: 1 container image changed. Deployment/stageproof-check/minio-operator.template.spec.containers[0] operator container moves from quay.io/minio/operator:v6.0.1 to quay.io/minio/operator:v7.1.1.

findings.detail: A rehearsal installs the chart into an empty cluster. It does not upgrade data that is already there. An empty-cluster result of 0 restarts does not mean an existing workload stayed up.
findings.message: This chart ships custom resource definitions, and the application it runs is changing. Custom resources that already exist on a real cluster are not in this check.

findings.detail: 1-line fixes -> Argo CD: `syncOptions: [ServerSideApply=true]` | Flux: `install/upgrade.crds: CreateReplace` | Helm v4: `helm upgrade --server-side` | kubectl: `kubectl apply --server-side -f crds/` (pass `--server-side-apply` if already enabled).
findings.message: CRD size is 414 KiB (>256 KiB client-side `last-applied-configuration` limit).
